extracted.intended_audience: publishers submitting previously published short fiction by African writers (and African writers/their agents/publishers)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for submitting previously published English-language short stories by African writers to the Caine Prize for African Writing, including eligibility, format, publication requirements, and evaluative aesthetic qualities derived from past winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: African writer (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: "African writer" = national of an African country, or a parent African by birth/nationality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who counts as an eligible author for the prize; parentage by birth/nationality qualifies even if the author is not currently resident in Africa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fictional short story requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only works of fiction are eligible; non-fiction and factual genres are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length (indicative)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a target word-count range for submissions; 'indicative' suggests some flexibility but this is the expected short-story length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of publication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted work must have been published in English (i.e., the published version is in English).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Published in the 5 years preceding deadline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only works published within the five years before the contest deadline are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously published; not self-published
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be previously published; not self-published
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work must have an established prior publication via a publisher (self-published works are explicitly ineligible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission source
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be made by the publisher rather than by the author themselves; procedural requirement for who may enter a work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Children's stories; Factual writing; Academic essays; Plays; Poetry; Autobiography/biography
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms are explicitly ineligible for the prize; they are listed as genre exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary craft
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for technical excellence at the level of sentence construction and prose craft; tight, well-crafted sentences are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong, individual narrative voice is prized; past winners frequently experiment with point of view or voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: **Place specificity** — African settings rendered with detail and refusal of cliché
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should render African settings with specificity and nuance, avoiding tired or reductive clichés.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance to single-narrative-Africa
rubrics_metrics.description: **Resistance to single-narrative-Africa** — the prize rewards work that complicates Western expectations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that challenges simplistic or monolithic portrayals of Africa and complicates Western expectations is favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political consciousness without polemic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political or social awareness in a story is welcome but should not be didactic or polemical; nuance is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: **Form innovation** — many winners take formal risks
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal experimentation and inventive structural choices are commonly present among winners; the prize rewards formal risk-taking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional weight
rubrics_metrics.description: **Emotional weight** — even short pieces carry significant gravity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should carry emotional impact and gravitas despite their short length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable winners' aesthetic range (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Realism (Helon Habila, Binyavanga Wainaina); Speculative (NoViolet Bulawayo); Fragmented/experimental (Henrietta Rose-Innes); Diasporic identity (Lesley Nneka Arimah)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of past winners indicate the breadth of acceptable aesthetics and genres — realism, speculative fiction, fragmented/experimental forms, and diasporic identity themes have all been successful.
